steps.title: Reject impossible file counts before reading

quiz.prompt: Which operation must wait until the outer count is accepted?

hints.text: Validate the length before following either input pointer.
Use an unsigned upper-bound comparison.

steps.title: Retain the two cursors and their remaining counts

quiz.prompt: What is read from descriptor offset zero?

hints.text: Retain the descriptor pointer separately from its capacity.
Native descriptor doublewords follow the selected target byte order.

steps.title: Assemble four file bytes into one number

quiz.prompt: Why use unsigned byte loads here?

choices.text: A file byte must contribute its value from 0 through 255.
PNG fields use target byte order.
Every PNG field is eight bytes wide.

hints.text: Shift the accumulated value before combining the next byte.
Do not sign-extend a byte whose high bit is set.

quiz.prompt: When may the file cursor advance past the signature?

choices.text: After checking only its first byte.
After any helper returns a nonzero number.

hints.text: Retain the original cursor across both helper calls.
Advance the cursor and remaining count by the same eight bytes.

steps.title: Prove that one complete chunk fits

quiz.prompt: What does the twelve-byte overhead contain?

choices.text: The signature and four pixel bytes.
Length, four type bytes and CRC.
Only the CRC repeated three times.

hints.text: Perform the minimum-size check before subtracting overhead.
Compare the decoded length against the remaining count, not the original file size.

quiz.prompt: Which original type byte carries the reserved case bit?

hints.text: ASCII letter validation and case-bit meaning are separate checks.
Use the original third byte for the reserved-bit test.

quiz.prompt: Which bytes does a zero count permit the CRC helper to read?

hints.text: The CRC byte loop must test its count before a load.
Keep the reflected polynomial and final complement consistent with the earlier CRC chapter.

steps.title: Check the type and payload together

quiz.prompt: Why retain the computed CRC before reading the stored CRC?

choices.text: Both helpers return through the same result register.
The stored CRC changes the file length.
Native descriptor byte order determines CRC coverage.

hints.text: The CRC covers four type bytes plus the payload.
Preserve a helper result before calling another helper that uses the same result register.

steps.title: Choose a type only after its CRC passes

quiz.prompt: Why does a valid IDAT checksum not suffice before IHDR?

choices.text: Chunk order is a separate format requirement.
IDAT is always an unknown critical type.
A checksum specifies the image dimensions.

hints.text: Recognize IHDR before applying the general header-seen requirement.
Keep type recognition separate from each handler’s length and ordering checks.

quiz.prompt: When are parsed dimensions published in the descriptor?

choices.text: After the whole accepted container reaches the publication region.

hints.text: Read dimensions as PNG fields and validate their numerical bounds.
Do not store successful output fields while later chunks can still fail.

quiz.prompt: How far does a chunk with one payload byte advance the file cursor?

hints.text: The next cursor follows the payload and its stored CRC.
Apply one extent to both the address and remaining count.

steps.title: Admit only a well-formed optional palette

quiz.prompt: What does a three-byte PLTE payload contain?

hints.text: Check both the ordering flags and the payload length.
A multiple of three is not sufficient if the length is zero.

steps.title: Distinguish skippable metadata from excluded features

quiz.prompt: What does an accepted non-IDAT chunk after IDAT establish?

choices.text: A later IDAT may restart the same consecutive group.
Its payload must be decoded as pixels.

hints.text: Recognized but unsupported image features have explicit rejection rules.
Preserve the difference between “IDAT has begun” and “its consecutive group has ended.”

quiz.prompt: When must the capacity check occur?

hints.text: Reserve a whole admitted payload before entering its byte loop.
An empty IDAT changes ordering state even though it copies no bytes.

steps.title: Join payload bytes without their envelopes

quiz.prompt: What follows the first copied 0x78 in the joined stream?

hints.text: The compressed output contains payload bytes only.
Keep the destination cursor across chunks; reset the source payload cursor for each one.

steps.title: Require a final empty IEND and enough joined bytes

quiz.prompt: What does collector success establish about DEFLATE?

choices.text: Every compressed symbol has been decoded.
The collected payload is ready for separate inflation checks.
Its Adler checksum is necessarily valid.

hints.text: A valid IEND CRC does not excuse trailing selected bytes.
The six-byte minimum is a wrapper-size bound, not decompression.

steps.title: Publish the completed container result together

quiz.prompt: Why is the predicted inflated count 35 rather than 30?

choices.text: Each of five rows includes one filter byte.
Every RGB sample has a padding byte.
The PNG signature has five bytes.

hints.text: Publish the result only after every admitted chunk has passed its checks.
The inflated row still contains its selector byte.
